referees.quote: what I find missing is the novelty from the manuscript... As a result, I cannot recommend this paper to Nature Communication.

More rigorous experimental evidence, or exclusions of alternative possibilities (e.g., YSR states), are needed. Therefore, I cannot recommend the publication of this manuscript in Nature Communications.
This study may be worth publishing in Nat. Commun., however, it is not easy to make this determination... several questions and comments which should be properly answered before I can make a decision

note: First round is Version 0 in this file; there is no sign of a transfer from another journal. No referee used the scale words, so all three recommendations are inferred. R1 and R2 are coded as reject because each says it 'cannot recommend' publication in Nature Communications: R1 on grounds of novelty, R2 because the topological origin is not established. R3 withheld a decision until substantive questions were answered, including distinguishing the observed states from Andreev bound states and YSR states, so R3 is coded as major revision. In later rounds R1 and R3 recommended publication in Version 1, and R2 recommended publication in Version 2.
